statement: What are all the solutions to the equation $x(x - 5) = 6$?

choices.misconception: I set each factor equal to $0$, as if the equation were $x(x - 5) = 0$, and ignored the $6$ on the right side.
I rewrote the equation as $x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0$ but factored it as $(x + 6)(x - 1)$, mixing up the signs.
I set each factor equal to $6$, solving $x = 6$ and $x - 5 = 6$, which gives $6$ and $11$.

hints: The zero product property only works when one side is $0$.
Expand the left side, subtract $6$, and factor.

solutions.reliable: Expand and move everything to one side: $x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0$. Factoring gives $(x - 6)(x + 1) = 0$, so $x = 6$ or $x = -1$. Check: $6(1) = 6$ and $(-1)(-6) = 6$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
